detail:
MedlinePlus describes CRPS management as multidisciplinary and generally more effective when started early, with goals of reducing pain and preserving or restoring use of the affected limb. Physical and occupational therapy are described as central to many care plans: therapists typically build programs around gentle, progressive movement, desensitization techniques for touch sensitivity, and exercises intended to maintain range of motion and function, because prolonged immobility is described in sources as worsening stiffness and weakness.

MedlinePlus notes that clinicians may discuss several medicine classes, including analgesics, anti-inflammatory medicines, corticosteroids, and classes also used for nerve-related pain, along with procedures such as sympathetic nerve blocks in selected cases. Some care plans also include psychological support for coping with chronic pain, stress, and reduced function. Sources present no single treatment as reliably effective for everyone, and care plans are usually adjusted over time based on pain, function, and side effects.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about managing complex regional pain syndrome.
summary: MedlinePlus describes CRPS management as multidisciplinary and best started early, centered on physical and occupational therapy to preserve limb use, with several medicine classes and procedures considered in selected cases.
takeaways: therapy to preserve movement and function is central in sources
therapists typically build in desensitization and progressive movement
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS): managing persistent limb pain day to day
